subject: random seed issue (for a single seed only)

messages.author: 38e260fc5780b4d6
messages.subject: random seed issue (for a single seed only)
parts:
Hi all,

When I use the flag random seed=4294967295, I do not get the same behavior each time (whereas I do for the other seeds I get/try). When this seed is used, I see a different seed number in my csv output file as well. I flukily noticed this using one of my models, so tried with the birats models posted in the Stan examples list (see: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/master/src/models/bugs_examples/vol2/birats) but still get this strange behavior. 

Is there something I am doing incorrectly that would make a single seed not work when others seem to? 

I am using CmdStan 2.1.0

To see this using birats, I can run:

./birats.exe sample num_warmup=20 num_samples=10 save_warmup=1 data file=birats.dump random seed=4294967295 output file=birats.csv

Cheers,
Andria

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] random seed issue (for a single seed only)
parts:
Hi Andria,

Odd, I can't seem to reproduce this with the current develop branch:

[mbrubake@structure birats]$ ./birats sample num_warmup=20 num_samples=10 save_warmup=1 data file=birats.data.R random seed=4294967295 output file=birats.csv
...
 random
   seed = 4294967295 (Default)
 output
   file = birats.csv
   diagnostic_file =  (Default)
   refresh = 100 (Default)
...

Anyway, you seem to have somehow managed to pick the seed which represents the largest value an unsigned 32-bit integer can take.  I.E., 4294967295 = 2^32 - 1.  This is most likely causing a bug somewhere either in parsing the number or in representing it.  We'll have to take a look, but I suspect that so long as you pick values less than that (or, in the worst case, less than 2^31 - 1 = 2,147,483,647) all will be well!

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] random seed issue (for a single seed only)
parts:
Thanks. I just opened an issue to fix the bug:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/521

The problem is almost certainly due to the fact that your
specified seed overflows a signed int. In fact,
the value is exactly the maximum value that will fit
into an unsigned int (2^32 - 1).

No idea why it's causing different behaviors across
runs.

- Bob
